basic shot seconds between volleys. On the music grid: 0.56625 is 2.265/4, one quarter note of CONFIG.music.barSeconds. Trying the slowest of the three candidates (bar/4, bar/6 = 0.3775, bar/8 = 0.28315) — this is 36% slower than the 0.36 it replaces, so read it against damagePerLevel before keeping it

basic shot damage per pellet at level 1, before weapon.damagePerLevel and before any card. Was 7.5 and had no row here at all — a saved snapshot was its only real home, so editing config.js could not move it. Read against enemies.csv hp (a starting fish is 6, +0.8 per difficulty) and against the whole arsenal in this file: at the shipped bar/4 cadence and two pellets this is the gun's entire opening dps

basic shot pebble SIZE — the hit circle and the drawn stone together. One number for both: main.js divides this by the pebble asset's authored radius (0.18) to get the mesh scale, so the stone is always drawn exactly as big as it hits. It used to normalise to the asset instead, which meant raising this widened the hitbox and changed nothing on screen. Was 0.18; against a starting fish's 0.4 this is a 14% wider hit window, and the shot travels 0.37 units a frame at 60fps so the margin is worth having

basic shot seconds a pellet flies — its RANGE, since range is life x speed. At the shipped speed of 22 this is 79 world units against an arena 80 wide, so a pellet now reaches the far wall; it was 1.6 (35 units), which is under half the screen and is why shots died in open water on a target the player could see. Andre 3000 multiplies this rather than replacing it, and every other projectile in the game carries its own life (CONFIG.missile.life, scallop.life, and so on) — this row is the GUN's.
shot grid: fire the basic shot on the music's bar lines. Off = the pre-grid free-running cooldown at the same interval
shot grid: the run's FIRST shot waits for a downbeat (up to one bar of no gun). Off = it waits for the next slot instead, like every re-lock after it
shot grid: finest division of a bar the interval may reach — a backstop against stacked halvings, not a balance number. 64 is 28 shots/sec

basic shot: the fins TRADE shots instead of firing together. On, one flipper per tick at fireRate / 2, so a bar/4 gun lands on eighth notes and the flashes read left-right-left. Off = the old simultaneous volley. Same pellets, same damage, same push either way — only the timing moves

Flippers Up!: how much fatter one stack makes the pebbles leaving ONE flipper. Compounds per stack on that side, and stacks alternate fins — so 6 stacks is 1.22^3 = 1.82x on both, not 1.22^6 on one. Radius AND the drawn stone; damage per pellet is untouched, so this buys reach. Read it against weapon.radius (0.18)

Flippers Up!: which stack first puts an ELEMENT on the fin it feeds. 2 = the opening pick is one stone and nothing else, and every stack after it lights or deepens the fin it grows. Set above the card maxStacks (6) to turn the element half off entirely and leave a pure size card

strike: what a PERFECT CHARGE multiplies that weak-spot bite by — the first thing the perfect latch has ever bought. On the beat without a perfect charge still bites, at 1x. At 2 a perfect full-charge ram is ~390 after hotSpots.critMul, about one rupture pool on a first boss

food chain: seconds without a mouthful before the chain lapses. THE number that decides whether a chain can be kept up — at 1.1 a link needed a strike every 1.5s (npm run sim:chain)

perfect charge: the fraction of a full bank that counts as perfectly loaded. The meter pops here and mechanics will be hung off it — below 1 the top of the bar becomes a window a player can hit early rather than a ceiling they hold against

sweet spot: how much error a release is allowed either side of the STRIKE NOW! moment, as a fraction of the wind-up. Inside it the strike deals its damage; outside it the dash is a pure speed boost. It no longer gates the food chain - a completed charge arms that at any timing - which is why it can afford to be tight. 0.04 on a 1s bar is 40ms either side, five frames at 60fps. Careful below this: the window quantizes to FRAMES, and 0.03 is three frames at 60fps and a single frame at 30

food chain: chum a sweet-spot strike must collect before it counts as a FOOD CHAIN. The strike arms it; the food scores it, and the number then ticks up one per pip eaten inside the window. 1 = hit the beat, eat one thing

food chain: how much the price of a link goes UP with each link already banked. 1 = link 1 costs linkMinPips mouthfuls, link 2 one more, link 3 two more — a x5 chain is 15 chum, not 5. Partial progress is banked and survives a release; it dies with the chain. 0 is the old flat rule, one mouthful one link
boost meter: pips a run OPENS with. 0 = a dead meter until the first mouthful, so the food chain is the only thing that fuels a strike. Set at or above the pip count to start full (the old behaviour)

the size of one breath, in points. Against a 5/sec deplete rate this is the seconds of dive it buys — 132 = 26.4s. Base for every Deep Lungs stack, and the ceiling Iron Lung's damage bonus is measured against — the bonus itself follows the CURRENT bar

how fast a breach refills the tank, per second above the water line — the only way air comes back other than a bubble. Against the 5/sec deplete it is the exchange rate of the whole dive: 52.5 buys 10.5 seconds of dive per second spent in the air, and refills a full 132-point breath in 2.5s. Was a slider, and a snapshot was holding it at 35 where config.js could not reach it

how many ambient bubbles the arena is never allowed to be short of. The floor, refilled on oxygen.bubbleRefillDelay rather than on the interval below — a run of unlucky interval rolls used to leave the floor with nothing on it for half a minute, and a pickup you cannot see is a pickup that does not exist

the cap on ambient bubbles up at once. The spawner will not top up past it and its clock HOLDS there rather than banking spawns — see stepBubbleSpawner in systems/oxygenBubble.js. Read against bubbleRefillAmount: at 30 points a bubble and 132 to a breath, two of them up is most of a tank sitting in the water

seconds before the floor replaces a bubble that was taken or burst, whenever the arena is under bubbleMinAlive. Long enough that the refill is not visible as a spawner repairing itself on the frame the pickup left

seconds between ambient bubble spawns while the arena is between the floor and the cap — the trip from one bubble up to two, which is the part that is meant to feel like weather. Below the floor bubbleRefillDelay overrides it; at the cap nothing spawns at all
the long end of that interval. Was 7-13 with no headcount at all, which averaged a bubble and a half against a 14-second life and delivered it as stretches of two and stretches of none

the seal's starting health. Read against the enemy toughness ramp (CONFIG.spawn.ramp) and player.hpPerLevel, not by eye — it is the survivability half of the same economy oxygen.max is the dive half of. Had no slider AND no CSV row, so the 100 sitting in imported-tuning.json was its only real home

mussel shells in a level-1 barrage

mussel ceiling on the bonus shells a charged release buys — one per whole pip spent, capped low so the card's own count (3 at one stack, 10 at five) stays the number the barrage reads as; a deep or chained bar adds a shell or two on top rather than doubling the flight
mussel direct hit damage per shell
mussel direct hit damage per shell per stack
mussel blast damage per shell. Worth more than the direct hit on purpose — a homing shell almost always finds a body, so the blast is what the barrage is actually for
mussel blast damage per shell per stack
mussel blast radius per shell
basic shot damage added per stack of Multishot, as a FRACTION of the gun's current damage — the gun's damage is a live stat that grows all run, so a flat step would be decisive early and nothing late
basic shot size added per stack of Multishot, as a fraction of the pellet's radius

how many stacks of Multishot the two rows above are paid out for. maxStacks is 99 for the pellet count; a compounding bonus over 99 stacks is a gun nobody tuned, so the curve stops here and everything past it is pellets

pellets the basic shot puts in the water per volley, across BOTH flippers — 2 is one stone out of each. Each one leaves on its own tick (see CONFIG.weapon.multishot and systems/shotGrid.js), so this is also how many notes a volley is subdivided into: 2 is a pair of eighths on the bar/4 cadence, 3 is a triplet, 4 is sixteenths. It is a starting count, not a cap — Pocket Full of Stones, levelling and bosses all add to it

the most ticks one volley may be dealt across. Past this the gun stops subdividing and extra pellets thicken the ticks it already has, fanned, the way every pellet used to. A musical limit rather than a technical one: the bar ladder would go on halving to bar/64, and a gun rattling thirty-seconds all run is a texture rather than a rhythm. 1 turns the stagger off outright

levels between the free pellets the gun grows on its own, so it keeps pace with the water without an upgrade pick. 4 and not the 8 it was because a pellet is half what it used to be — multishot counts the whole volley now rather than one flipper's share — so this is the same stones per level, arriving one at a time
homing mussel damage added per stack. Small on purpose — the count is still what the card sells, this is the floor under it so fifteen stacks is not fifteen of the same shell
homing mussel size added per stack, as a fraction of its radius. Fractional because the radius is a tuner slider and a flat step would mean something different in every session
shrimp contact damage added per stack. A ring that is failing to kill something otherwise just gets more shrimp bouncing off it
shrimp size added per stack, as a fraction of scale. The contact reach is derived from the drawn size, so this buys reach as well as picture
scallop damage added per stack
scallop size added per stack, as a fraction of its radius — a bigger shell finds more on its way around, which is what the bounces are for

ricochet damage added per stack. This card already bought fire rate, lifespan and bounces; a longer combo made of chips is still chips — so the pellet itself climbs, and bounce.comboDamageStep then multiplies whatever it climbed to
ricochet size added per stack, as a fraction of its radius — a fatter shot finds its next body sooner, so the bounce budget is worth more rather than longer

basic shot pellets granted for every boss the run kills, permanently and automatically. The bosses' half of the baseline growth levelsPerExtraShot does for levels — a run four bosses deep fires eight more pellets whether or not it ever saw a Multishot card. Does NOT count as a stack of Multishot, so it buys no damage or size curve. 2 and not 1 because a pellet is half what it was: multishot is the whole volley now rather than one flipper's share, so this pays the same stones per boss it always did. 0 turns it off

how often a run starts as the pebble gun, against the other loadouts. 0 removes it from the roll entirely without deleting the block. Read this against a run's actual performance rather than by taste — the whole point of it being here
...and the fin lasers. Even at 1/1 while there are two: the laser is a different game rather than a harder or easier one, and a run should get either

bolt speed, against the pebble's 22. Half of the range: range is speed x life, and 1.9 x 0.34 puts a bolt at 51 units against the pebble's 79 — just over half the arena, arriving in half the time. Do not raise this to buy reach — that is what the ramp is for, and a faster bolt changes how much lead a moving fish needs

seconds a bolt flies, against the pebble's 3.6 (the shipped row above, NOT the 1.6 fallback in config.js). The other half of the range and the one the reach ramp moves, deliberately: lengthening the flight changes only how far it goes, where speeding it up changes how the weapon is aimed
what a bolt hits for, against the pebble. 1 on purpose — the reach is the whole price of this loadout and a second cost hidden here would make the laser strictly worse than the gun it replaces
gun cards per step of reach earned back. Counts family:'gun' picks off the whole run, so a new gun card counts without anyone adding it to a list
what one step is worth, as a fraction of the bolt's flight time. Five steps at 0.15 is 1.75x — 90 units against the pebble's 79, past it, which is the payoff for having gone all in on the gun
the ceiling on those steps. A cap and not a target

whether any of the ramp is paid before the run's first boss is down. 1 (the shipped state) makes the boss a GATE: a run holding twenty gun stacks with no boss killed is on step 0, and every step it already qualified for lands the moment one dies
how much wider one EVEN stack of André 3000 fans the volley, on a laser loadout. Odd stacks buy pierce instead — the card alternates. Multiplies the fan whether the rig has fins or not

stacks of Pocket Full of Stones that still buy a BOLT before the card converts to buying splits. 1: the opening stack is the second bolt the player expects, and every stack after it is lattice. At 0 the first pick reads as having done nothing
chance a bolt shatters on the body it hits. A third is often enough to be the weapon's identity and rare enough that a bolt landing plainly is still the normal case

shards on the FIRST split, before Pocket Full of Stones adds to it. Read this against childrenDecay and generationsMax together — the three of them are what stops the shatter going exponential, and none of them is safe to raise alone
shards LOST per generation, floored at 1. Guard 1 of 3: without it the count is children^generations, which at 4 wide and 3 deep is 64 bolts off one pellet several times a second
how deep the shatter goes before any pierce is bought. 1 is one split and no re-splitting
stacks of pierce per extra generation. Guard 2 of 3, and the conservative half of it: pierce is bought one odd stack of André 3000 at a time, so 2 here is four picks per level of depth
the hard ceiling on depth. The other half of guard 2. A cap, not a target

shards born of a split that may be in the water at once. Guard 3 of 3, and the one that holds when the first two are retuned by somebody who has not read systems/finLaser.js. A split that would cross it is refused WHOLE rather than trimmed — half a lattice reads as the effect being broken
what a shard hits for, as a fraction of its parent. Compounds down the generations, which is what keeps a third-generation shard a spark rather than a third gun
...and how fast it goes. Compounds the same way
...and how long it lives, which is why a deep shatter stays local instead of raking the arena. Compounds
...and how big it is, hitbox and drawn body together. Compounds
half-angle of the shard fan, in radians, about the PARENT's heading — so a shatter carries on through the body rather than spraying back off it

seconds a shard ignores bodies for. NOT the guard against re-hitting what the parent hit — that is the copied hit set in trySplit. This is only so two shards born on the same frame do not both resolve inside one creature before either has moved

the ceiling on how much Pocket Full of Stones may widen the FIRST split. The other half of guard 1, and the number the worst case turns on: at 2 the widest split is 4 and a full three-generation shatter is 40 shards against a budget of 48. At 3 it is 78 and the budget starts refusing. A stack past this goes back to buying bolts rather than doing nothing
